messages.content:
Risk: Lack of transparency
Description: Challenges in understanding or explaining the decision-making processes of AI systems, which can lead to mistrust, difficulty in enforcing compliance standards or holding relevant actors accountable for harms, and the inability to identify and correct errors.
Concern: None
Policy: Clinical Diagnosis & Treatment Recommendations

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0047: AI-Enabled Product or Service - ATLAS — Adversaries may use a product or service that uses artificial intelligence under the hood to gain access to the underlying AI model.
This type of indirect model access may reveal details of the AI model or its inferences in logs or metadata. [found by 6/15 queries]
  Siblings: AI Model Inference API Access - ATLAS, Physical Environment Access - ATLAS, Full AI Model Access - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.TA0000: AI Model Access - ATLAS — The adversary is attempting to gain some level of access to an AI model.

AI Model Access enables techniques that use various types of access to the AI model that can be used by the adversary to gain information, develop attacks, and as a means to input data to the model.
The level of access can range from the full knowledge of the internals of the model to access to the physical environment where data is collected for use in the AI model.
The adversary may use varying levels of model access during the course of their attack, from staging the attack to impacting the target system.

Access to an AI model may require access to the system housing the model, the model may be publicly accessible via an API, or it may be accessed indirectly via interaction with a product or service that utilizes AI as part of its processes. [found by 6/15 queries]
  Siblings: Command and Control - ATTACK Mobile, Defense Evasion - SPARTA, Lateral Movement - ATTACK Mobile
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0063: Discover AI Model Outputs - ATLAS — Adversaries may discover model outputs, such as class scores, whose presence is not required for the system to function and are not intended for use by the end user. Model outputs may be found in logs or may be included in API responses.
Model outputs may enable the adversary to identify weaknesses in the model and develop attacks. [found by 6/15 queries]
  Siblings: Discover AI Model Family - ATLAS, Process Discovery - ATLAS, Discover AI Model Ontology - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0024: Exfiltration via AI Inference API - ATLAS — Adversaries may exfiltrate private information via [AI Model Inference API Access](/techniques/AML.T0040).
AI Models have been shown leak private information about their training data (e.g.  [Infer Training Data Membership](/techniques/AML.T0024.000), [Invert AI Model](/techniques/AML.T0024.001)).
The model itself may also be extracted ([Extract AI Model](/techniques/AML.T0024.002)) for the purposes of [AI Intellectual Property Theft](/techniques/AML.T0048.004).

Exfiltration of information relating to private training data raises privacy concerns.
Private training data may include personally identifiable information, or other protected data. [found by 6/15 queries]
  Siblings: LLM Response Rendering - ATLAS, Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation - ATLAS, LLM Data Leakage - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0010.001: AI Software - ATLAS — Most AI systems rely on a limited set of AI frameworks.
An adversary could get access to a large number of AI systems through a comprise of one of their supply chains.
Many AI projects also rely on other open source implementations of various algorithms.
These can also be compromised in a targeted way to get access to specific systems. [found by 5/15 queries]
  Siblings: Hardware - ATLAS, Data - ATLAS, Container Registry - ATLAS

axes.rationale: Lack of transparency often stems from limited access to the AI model itself. Understanding how the model works requires access to its structure, parameters, and decision-making processes.
Transparency is hindered when the outputs of the AI model are not readily available or interpretable.  Discovering these outputs can shed light on the model's reasoning and potential biases.
